hints: For a rectangle whose height is exactly heights[i], how far can it stretch left and right?
It stretches until the first shorter bar on each side. Finding those for every i is a 'next smaller element' problem.
Keep a stack of increasing heights. When a shorter bar arrives, pop taller bars - each popped bar's rectangle ends here.

insight.mnemonic: A shorter bar closes every taller rectangle still open.
insight.oneLiner: Every bar's best rectangle spans until the next shorter bar on each side; an increasing stack finds both edges as bars are popped.
insight.pattern: Monotonic stack (next smaller on both sides)

recall.a: The rectangle of the popped bar's height from its start up to (not including) i.
Everything popped was taller, so the new bar's rectangle can extend left over them.
recall.q: Why does the new bar inherit the popped start?

signals: maximal rectangle in a matrix (row by row)
insight.why: When bar i pops a taller bar, i is that bar's first shorter neighbour on the right, and its stored start is its left edge. Each bar is pushed and popped once: O(n).

oneLiner: Every bar's best rectangle spans until the next shorter bar on each side; an increasing stack finds both edges as bars are popped.

pitfalls.explain: Bars still on the stack at the end extend all the way to the right edge - compute their rectangles too.
pitfalls.title: Forgot the bars left on the stack

pitfalls.explain: After popping taller bars, the new bar's rectangle starts at the last popped start, not at i.
pitfalls.title: Didn't extend the new bar's start

solutions.idea: For each left edge, extend right while maintaining the minimum height.
solutions.name: Every range, tracking its minimum

footnotes.text: Popping a taller bar finalizes its rectangle (its right edge is i). The new, shorter bar inherits the popped start: its own rectangle can extend left over everything that was taller.

solutions.idea: Keep bars in increasing height; popping a bar finalizes the widest rectangle of its height.
solutions.name: Monotonic stack

starter:
class Solution:
    def largestRectangleArea(self, heights: List[int]) -> int:
statement:
`heights[i]` is the height of bar `i` in a histogram; every bar has width 1. Return the **area of the largest rectangle** that fits entirely inside the histogram.

A rectangle spanning bars `l..r` can be at most as tall as the shortest bar in that range.
title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
